title: Record ADRs: storage and key custody, threat model, profile authority
description: Spec §15 asks for short decisions before implementation. These are also the design questions opum-agent records in opum-doc (vault format, keychain binding, plugin name); the ADRs here are this repo's position to argue there.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Lore ADRs exist for vault format/key custody, the P0 threat model and non-guarantees, and profile approval authority

implementationNotes: Drafted the three ADRs (docs/adr/0001-0003) from the orchestrator's 2026-09-28 ruling on the design questions. Q1: vault format version 1 adopted as WCLI-4 implements it; rollback is not detected; any change to the AAD needs a new format version. Q2: a generic-password item (service opum.ward, account derived from the vault ID) via @napi-rs/keyring. The ACL is per-build and ad-hoc signed, and is not a security boundary. Developer ID signing is deferred past P0 and held by the operator, as the precondition for any ACL claim. WCLI-19 is accepted as a stated P0 limitation. The legacy-versus-data-protection keychain question is recorded as open and unmeasured, and added to WCLI-5 as acceptance criterion 4, with the real-keychain write left for the developer to authorise at that task's start. WCLI-5 also gained criterion 5, a bounded noninteractive failure. Q3: plugin name opum-ward. The ADRs bind only once opum-doc records the decision. Its record id is pending, so the placeholder ODOC-PENDING must be replaced before the PR lands. ADR 0003 (profile authority) restates spec §2, §4.3 and §9.2 rather than a new ruling.

Orchestrator follow-up, 2026-09-28: ADR 0003 needs no opum-doc record, so it now says it restates the spec and cites none. ADRs 0001 and 0002 cite opum-agent OPAG-672 (verified To Do on opum-agent's origin/dev; opum-ai/opum-agent#1248 merged) for the Developer ID signing decision. Only 0001 and 0002 still carry ODOC-PENDING.
